The two entries stated the same fact and were both right about it; the inconsistency was in how the register labelled it, and the wording was too loose. The register is amended at the same link: https://claude.ai/artifact/KyDJAbbXP3dFR9HRjxitbu

Returned goods that have already shipped are not put back into stock, and that is deliberate. Saleor's fulfillment guide says returns "require manual stock restoration after staff review", and the order-status page says "Returning items will not modify stock". It is still a problem for your staff, so it now appears once, in ST-12, as a designed-in limitation.

"Returns never restock" was imprecise, though. This is what the code does; I read it but did not run it against a database:

| Action | On hand | Reserved for the order |
|---|---|---|
| Return or replace shipped units | Unchanged | Unchanged |
| Return, refund or replace units not yet shipped (legacy mutations) | Unchanged | Released |
| Return or refund units in a fulfillment waiting for approval | Unchanged | Stays held and is never released |
| Refund money only (granted refund, transaction refund, `orderRefund`, `paymentRefund`) | Unchanged | Unchanged |
| Cancel a shipped fulfillment | Added back, in whichever warehouse staff name | Reserved again for the same order |
| Cancel a fulfillment waiting for approval | Unchanged | Still held |
| Cancel the order, or let it expire | Unchanged | Everything left is released |

Cancelling the order is refused while a shipped or waiting fulfillment remains. The full table, with the fulfilled-count column, is on the page under "Stock flow when an order is unwound".

Changes to the register:

- **ST-12 (rewritten):** shipped returns leave stock untouched by design, the return input has no warehouse field, and nothing records which returns were put back. Staff must correct stock by hand through the absolute-overwrite edit in ST-4.
- **RR-14 (amended):** the restock line is removed and replaced with a pointer to ST-12, RR-8 and RR-15.
- **RR-8 (re-checked and sharpened):** returning or refunding a line that is waiting for approval leaves its stock reserved. If the order also has shipped fulfillments, nothing can release it.
- **RR-15 (new):** refunding money never releases stock or stops a line being shipped. A line refunded before shipping stays in the to-fulfill list with its stock held.
- **FU-13 (new):** a refunded, returned or replaced fulfillment can itself be cancelled. That adds stock, reopens the line for shipping, and reverses no money.
- **FU-14 (new):** cancelling a fulfillment restocks into any warehouse named, without checking it against the source warehouse or the channel. It can also add units the original fulfillment never deducted.

The register now has 97 entries, 51 of them re-checked; the three new ones are all medium severity. I could not check whether the dashboard offers a cancel button on returned or refunded fulfillments (FU-13), because the dashboard is not in this repository.

Sources:
- [Order Fulfillment](https://docs.saleor.io/developer/order/order-fulfillment)
- [Order Status](https://docs.saleor.io/developer/checkout/order-status)
- [Stock Overview](https://docs.saleor.io/developer/stock/overview)

2

5	For the high-volume async events (orders, draft orders, fulfillments, checkouts, per-channel
6	stock and discounted-price changes) the subscription-webhook payload is not built in the request
7	that triggered the event. The request records only a pointer (the object's identity, the
8	requestor and the request time), creates `PENDING` deliveries with no payload, and enqueues a
9	background task. That task re-reads the object and resolves the subscription query against the
10	database as it is at that moment. Whether an event is deferred is a per-event flag in
11	`WebhookEventAsyncType.EVENT_MAP`.
12	
13	The motivation is request latency. Resolving a subscription query for a large order means
14	running GraphQL resolvers, dataloaders and often sync webhook calls such as tax calculation, and
15	doing that once per subscribed app inside the mutation made the heaviest order and checkout
16	mutations noticeably slower. Moving it to a worker keeps the mutation's cost independent of how
17	many apps subscribe and how deep their queries are.
18	
19	The accepted consequence is that an async webhook is a notification that something happened,
20	carrying the object's current state, not a snapshot of the state at the time it happened. If a
21	field was `A` when the mutation ran and `B` by the time the task runs, every pending delivery for
22	that object carries `B`. Two mutations in quick succession produce two deliveries that are
23	indistinguishable to the receiver. If the object is deleted before the task runs, the deliveries
24	are marked `FAILED` and no webhook is sent. Consumers that need the previous value must keep it
25	themselves. The snapshot alternative, serializing the payload in the request and storing it, is
26	exactly the cost the decision removes, so it was rejected rather than offered as an opt-in.
27	
28	This applies to subscription webhooks only. Legacy webhooks without a subscription query still
29	serialize their payload inline and therefore do see the request-time state. The same event can
30	reach a legacy receiver with `A` and a subscription receiver with `B`.
31	
32	The task reads from the read replica, and the replica may lag behind the write that created the
33	deliveries. Instead of reading from the writer, the task waits: it checks that the delivery rows
34	are visible on the replica and retries with backoff until they are, pinning the check and the
35	payload generation to a single replica connection so they see one snapshot. Reading from the
36	writer would move the full payload-generation load onto the primary, which is the database that
37	every pod shares and the scaling bottleneck.
38	
39	## Per-webhook opt-out
40	
41	Deferral is right by default but not for every consumer. An integration that applies each
42	`ORDER_METADATA_UPDATED` in sequence, expecting the metadata as written by each request, breaks
43	when several pending deliveries all carry the final state. Each webhook therefore carries a
44	`payloadGeneration` choice, `DEFERRED` by default or `IMMEDIATE`, set by the app that registers it
45	through the mutations or the manifest. An `IMMEDIATE` subscription webhook on a deferred event has
46	its payload built by whatever triggered the event, as every webhook did before deferral, and only
47	that webhook pays the cost. For events fired from a request that is the mutation's latency. For
48	events fired from a background task, such as the variant price and stock events, it is that task's
49	run time, which is why those events were deferred from the start. An app that sets `IMMEDIATE` on
50	such an event takes that cost knowingly. Because such a task may fire the event with a replica-allowed
51	manager right after its own write, an `IMMEDIATE` payload on a deferrable event is resolved against the
52	writer, so the dataloader-resolved fields cannot predate the write. Fields read from the subscribable
53	object itself still reflect where the caller loaded it from. The choice is ignored where it cannot apply: legacy
54	webhooks without a subscription query, sync events, and events that are not deferred.
55	
56	## When each event became deferred

59	generation-time state depends on the event. Dates are merge dates on `main`. The release is the

62	| Event | Deferred since | Release | Change |

70

72	order events on 2026-02-17 and reverted to inline on 2026-04-02 (#19012), before 3.23.0 was

# Deferred webhook payloads reflect state at generation time, not at trigger time

**Tags:** webhook, orders, checkout, concurrency

For the high-volume async events (orders, draft orders, fulfillments, checkouts, per-channel
stock and discounted-price changes) the subscription-webhook payload is not built in the request
that triggered the event. The request records only a pointer (the object's identity, the
requestor and the request time), creates `PENDING` deliveries with no payload, and enqueues a
background task. That task re-reads the object and resolves the subscription query against the
database as it is at that moment. Whether an event is deferred is a per-event flag in
`WebhookEventAsyncType.EVENT_MAP`.

The motivation is request latency. Resolving a subscription query for a large order means
running GraphQL resolvers, dataloaders and often sync webhook calls such as tax calculation, and
doing that once per subscribed app inside the mutation made the heaviest order and checkout
mutations noticeably slower. Moving it to a worker keeps the mutation's cost independent of how
many apps subscribe and how deep their queries are.

The accepted consequence is that an async webhook is a notification that something happened,
carrying the object's current state, not a snapshot of the state at the time it happened. If a
field was `A` when the mutation ran and `B` by the time the task runs, every pending delivery for
that object carries `B`. Two mutations in quick succession produce two deliveries that are
indistinguishable to the receiver. If the object is deleted before the task runs, the deliveries
are marked `FAILED` and no webhook is sent. Consumers that need the previous value must keep it
themselves. The snapshot alternative, serializing the payload in the request and storing it, is
exactly the cost the decision removes, so it was rejected rather than offered as an opt-in.

This applies to subscription webhooks only. Legacy webhooks without a subscription query still
serialize their payload inline and therefore do see the request-time state. The same event can
reach a legacy receiver with `A` and a subscription receiver with `B`.

The task reads from the read replica, and the replica may lag behind the write that created the
deliveries. Instead of reading from the writer, the task waits: it checks that the delivery rows
are visible on the replica and retries with backoff until they are, pinning the check and the
payload generation to a single replica connection so they see one snapshot. Reading from the
writer would move the full payload-generation load onto the primary, which is the database that
every pod shares and the scaling bottleneck.

## Per-webhook opt-out

Deferral is right by default but not for every consumer. An integration that applies each
`ORDER_METADATA_UPDATED` in sequence, expecting the metadata as written by each request, breaks
when several pending deliveries all carry the final state. Each webhook therefore carries a
`payloadGeneration` choice, `DEFERRED` by default or `IMMEDIATE`, set by the app that registers it
through the mutations or the manifest. An `IMMEDIATE` subscription webhook on a deferred event has
its payload built by whatever triggered the event, as every webhook did before deferral, and only
that webhook pays the cost. For events fired from a request that is the mutation's latency. For
events fired from a background task, such as the variant price and stock events, it is that task's
run time, which is why those events were deferred from the start. An app that sets `IMMEDIATE` on
such an event takes that cost knowingly. Because such a task may fire the event with a replica-allowed
manager right after its own write, an `IMMEDIATE` payload on a deferrable event is resolved against the
writer, so the dataloader-resolved fields cannot predate the write. Fields read from the subscribable
object itself still reflect where the caller loaded it from. The choice is ignored where it cannot apply: legacy
webhooks without a subscription query, sync events, and events that are not deferred.

## When each event became deferred

Deferral was rolled out event by event, so the version in which a consumer starts seeing
generation-time state depends on the event. Dates are merge dates on `main`. The release is the
first tagged version that ships the change.

| Event | Deferred since | Release | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CHECKOUT_CREATED`, `CHECKOUT_UPDATED` | 2024-11-15 | 3.21.0 | Introduced the mechanism (#16999) |
| `ORDER_CREATED`, `ORDER_CONFIRMED`, `ORDER_PAID`, `ORDER_FULLY_PAID`, `ORDER_REFUNDED`, `ORDER_FULLY_REFUNDED`, `ORDER_UPDATED`, `ORDER_CANCELLED`, `ORDER_EXPIRED`, `ORDER_FULFILLED`, `ORDER_METADATA_UPDATED` | 2026-02-17 | 3.23.0 | Moved from inline to deferred (#18809) |
| `DRAFT_ORDER_CREATED`, `DRAFT_ORDER_UPDATED` | 2026-02-17 | 3.23.0 | Moved from inline to deferred (#18809) |
| `FULFILLMENT_CANCELED`, `FULFILLMENT_METADATA_UPDATED`, `FULFILLMENT_TRACKING_NUMBER_UPDATED` | 2026-02-17 | 3.23.0 | Moved from inline to deferred (#18809) |
| `PRODUCT_VARIANT_DISCOUNTED_PRICE_UPDATED` | 2026-03-31 | 3.23.0, backported to 3.22.45 | New event, deferred from the start (#19004, #18973) |
| `PRODUCT_VARIANT_OUT_OF_STOCK_IN_CHANNEL`, `PRODUCT_VARIANT_BACK_IN_STOCK_IN_CHANNEL`, `PRODUCT_VARIANT_OUT_OF_STOCK_FOR_CLICK_AND_COLLECT`, `PRODUCT_VARIANT_BACK_IN_STOCK_FOR_CLICK_AND_COLLECT` | 2026-04-21 | 3.23.2 | New events, deferred from the start (#19144) |

`FULFILLMENT_CREATED` and `FULFILLMENT_APPROVED` were flagged as deferred together with the other
order events on 2026-02-17 and reverted to inline on 2026-04-02 (#19012), before 3.23.0 was
released. Their subscribable object is a plain dict rather than a model or a registered dataclass,
so it cannot be reconstructed in the task. No released version delivers them deferred.

Everything not listed, including `ORDER_BULK_CREATED`, `DRAFT_ORDER_DELETED` and all events
outside orders, checkout and variant stock or price, still builds its payload inline and carries
request-time state.

1	# Deferred webhook payloads reflect state at generation time, not at trigger time
2	
3	**Tags:** webhook, orders, checkout, concurrency
4	
5	For the high-volume async events (orders, draft orders, fulfillments, checkouts, per-channel
6	stock and discounted-price changes) the subscription-webhook payload is not built in the request
7	that triggered the event. The request records only a pointer (the object's identity, the
8	requestor and the request time), creates `PENDING` deliveries with no payload, and enqueues a
9	background task. That task re-reads the object and resolves the subscription query against the
10	database as it is at that moment. Whether an event is deferred is a per-event flag in
11	`WebhookEventAsyncType.EVENT_MAP`.
12	
13	The motivation is request latency. Resolving a subscription query for a large order means
14	running GraphQL resolvers, dataloaders and often sync webhook calls such as tax calculation, and
15	doing that once per subscribed app inside the mutation made the heaviest order and checkout
16	mutations noticeably slower. Moving it to a worker keeps the mutation's cost independent of how
17	many apps subscribe and how deep their queries are.
18	
19	The accepted consequence is that an async webhook is a notification that something happened,
20	carrying the object's current state, not a snapshot of the state at the time it happened. If a
21	field was `A` when the mutation ran and `B` by the time the task runs, every pending delivery for
22	that object carries `B`. Two mutations in quick succession produce two deliveries that are
23	indistinguishable to the receiver. If the object is deleted before the task runs, the deliveries
24	are marked `FAILED` and no webhook is sent. Consumers that need the previous value must keep it
25	themselves. The snapshot alternative, serializing the payload in the request and storing it, is
26	exactly the cost the decision removes, so it was rejected rather than offered as an opt-in.
27	
28	This applies to subscription webhooks only. Legacy webhooks without a subscription query still
29	serialize their payload inline and therefore do see the request-time state. The same event can
30	reach a legacy receiver with `A` and a subscription receiver with `B`.
31	
32	The task reads from the read replica, and the replica may lag behind the write that created the
33	deliveries. Instead of reading from the writer, the task waits: it checks that the delivery rows
34	are visible on the replica and retries with backoff until they are, pinning the check and the
35	payload generation to a single replica connection so they see one snapshot. Reading from the
36	writer would move the full payload-generation load onto the primary, which is the database that
37	every pod shares and the scaling bottleneck.
38	
39	## Per-webhook opt-out
40	
41	Deferral is right by default but not for every consumer. An integration that applies each
42	`ORDER_METADATA_UPDATED` in sequence, expecting the metadata as written by each request, breaks
43	when several pending deliveries all carry the final state. Each webhook therefore carries a
44	`payloadGeneration` choice, `DEFERRED` by default or `IMMEDIATE`, set by the app that registers it
45	through the mutations or the manifest. An `IMMEDIATE` subscription webhook on a deferred event has
46	its payload built by whatever triggered the event, as every webhook did before deferral, and only
47	that webhook pays the cost. For events fired from a request that is the mutation's latency. For
48	events fired from a background task, such as the variant price and stock events, it is that task's
49	run time, which is why those events were deferred from the start. An app that sets `IMMEDIATE` on
50	such an event takes that cost knowingly. Because such a task may fire the event with a replica-allowed
51	manager right after its own write, an `IMMEDIATE` payload on a deferrable event is resolved against the
52	writer, so the dataloader-resolved fields cannot predate the write. Fields read from the subscribable
53	object itself still reflect where the caller loaded it from. The choice is ignored where it cannot apply: legacy
54	webhooks without a subscription query, sync events, and events that are not deferred.
55	
56	## When each event became deferred
57	
58	Deferral was rolled out event by event, so the version in which a consumer starts seeing
59	generation-time state depends on the event. Dates are merge dates on `main`. The release is the
60	first tagged version that ships the change.
61	
62	| Event | Deferred since | Release | Change |
63	|---|---|---|---|
64	| `CHECKOUT_CREATED`, `CHECKOUT_UPDATED` | 2024-11-15 | 3.21.0 | Introduced the mechanism (#16999) |
65	| `ORDER_CREATED`, `ORDER_CONFIRMED`, `ORDER_PAID`, `ORDER_FULLY_PAID`, `ORDER_REFUNDED`, `ORDER_FULLY_REFUNDED`, `ORDER_UPDATED`, `ORDER_CANCELLED`, `ORDER_EXPIRED`, `ORDER_FULFILLED`, `ORDER_METADATA_UPDATED` | 2026-02-17 | 3.23.0 | Moved from inline to deferred (#18809) |
66	| `DRAFT_ORDER_CREATED`, `DRAFT_ORDER_UPDATED` | 2026-02-17 | 3.23.0 | Moved from inline to deferred (#18809) |
67	| `FULFILLMENT_CANCELED`, `FULFILLMENT_METADATA_UPDATED`, `FULFILLMENT_TRACKING_NUMBER_UPDATED` | 2026-02-17 | 3.23.0 | Moved from inline to deferred (#18809) |
68	| `PRODUCT_VARIANT_DISCOUNTED_PRICE_UPDATED` | 2026-03-31 | 3.23.0, backported to 3.22.45 | New event, deferred from the start (#19004, #18973) |
69	| `PRODUCT_VARIANT_OUT_OF_STOCK_IN_CHANNEL`, `PRODUCT_VARIANT_BACK_IN_STOCK_IN_CHANNEL`, `PRODUCT_VARIANT_OUT_OF_STOCK_FOR_CLICK_AND_COLLECT`, `PRODUCT_VARIANT_BACK_IN_STOCK_FOR_CLICK_AND_COLLECT` | 2026-04-21 | 3.23.2 | New events, deferred from the start (#19144) |
70	
71	`FULFILLMENT_CREATED` and `FULFILLMENT_APPROVED` were flagged as deferred together with the other
72	order events on 2026-02-17 and reverted to inline on 2026-04-02 (#19012), before 3.23.0 was
73	released. Their subscribable object is a plain dict rather than a model or a registered dataclass,
74	so it cannot be reconstructed in the task. No released version delivers them deferred.
75	
76	Everything not listed, including `ORDER_BULK_CREATED`, `DRAFT_ORDER_DELETED` and all events
77	outside orders, checkout and variant stock or price, still builds its payload inline and carries
78	request-time state.

def create_deliveries_for_subscriptions(
    event_type: str,
    subscribable_object,
    webhooks: Sequence["Webhook"],
    requestor=None,
    allow_replica=False,
    pre_save_payloads: dict | None = None,
    request_time: datetime.datetime | None = None,
) -> list[EventDelivery]:
    """Create a list of event deliveries with payloads based on subscription query.

    It uses a subscription query, defined for webhook to explicitly determine
    what fields should be included in the payload.

    :param event_type: event type which should be triggered.
    :param subscribable_object: subscribable object to process via subscription query.
    :param webhooks: sequence of async webhooks.
    :param requestor: used in subscription webhooks to generate meta data for payload.
    :return: List of event deliveries to send via webhook tasks.
    :param allow_replica: use replica database.
    """
    return create_deliveries_for_multiple_subscription_objects(
        event_type,
        [subscribable_object],
        webhooks,
        requestor,
        allow_replica,
        pre_save_payloads,
        request_time,
    ).get()


def create_deliveries_for_deferred_payload_subscriptions(
    event_type: str,
    subscribable_objects,
    webhooks: Sequence["Webhook"],
    requestor=None,
    allow_replica=False,
    request_time=None,
) -> dict[Hashable, list[tuple[EventDelivery, DeferredPayloadData]]]:
    deliveries_to_create = []
    deliveries_per_object: dict[
        Hashable, list[tuple[EventDelivery, DeferredPayloadData]]
    ] = defaultdict(list)

    for subscribable_object in subscribable_objects:
        deferred_payload_data = prepare_deferred_payload_data(
            subscribable_object=subscribable_object,
            requestor=requestor,
            request_time=request_time,
        )

        for webhook in webhooks:
            delivery = EventDelivery(
                status=EventDeliveryStatus.PENDING,
                event_type=event_type,
                webhook=webhook,
            )
            deliveries_to_create.append(delivery)
            deliveries_per_object[subscribable_object.pk].append(
                (delivery, deferred_payload_data)
            )

    EventDelivery.objects.bulk_create(deliveries_to_create)
    return deliveries_per_object


def group_webhooks_by_subscription(
    webhooks: Sequence["Webhook"],
) -> tuple[list["Webhook"], list["Webhook"]]:
    """Group webhooks by subscription query.

    Returns a tuple of two lists: legacy webhooks and subscription webhooks.
    """
    subscription = [webhook for webhook in webhooks if webhook.subscription_query]
    legacy = [webhook for webhook in webhooks if not webhook.subscription_query]
    return legacy, subscription


def group_subscription_webhooks_by_payload_generation(
    webhooks: Sequence["Webhook"],
) -> tuple[list["Webhook"], list["Webhook"]]:
    """Group subscription webhooks by their `payload_generation` setting.

    Returns a tuple of two lists: webhooks whose payload is built in the deferred
    task and webhooks whose payload is built immediately, in the request.
    """
    deferred = [
        webhook
        for webhook in webhooks
        if webhook.payload_generation == WebhookPayloadGeneration.DEFERRED
    ]
    immediate = [
        webhook
        for webhook in webhooks
        if webhook.payload_generation != WebhookPayloadGeneration.DEFERRED
    ]
    return deferred, immediate


@allow_writer()
def create_event_delivery_list_for_webhooks(
    webhooks: Sequence["Webhook"],
    event_payload: "EventPayload",
    event_type: str,
) -> list[EventDelivery]:
    event_deliveries = EventDelivery.objects.bulk_create(
        [
            EventDelivery(
                status=EventDeliveryStatus.PENDING,
                event_type=event_type,
                payload=event_payload,
                webhook=webhook,
            )
            for webhook in webhooks
        ]
    )
    return event_deliveries

def confirm_event_delivery_availability(
    event_delivery_ids: list[int],
    db_connection_name: str,
) -> tuple[set[int], set[int]]:
    """Confirm which event deliveries are available on the given DB connection."""
    available_delivery_pks = set(
        EventDelivery.objects.using(db_connection_name)
        .filter(pk__in=event_delivery_ids)
        .values_list("pk", flat=True)
    )

    missing_delivery_pks = set(event_delivery_ids) - available_delivery_pks
    return available_delivery_pks, missing_delivery_pks


@app.task(
    bind=True,
    max_retries=12,
)
@allow_writer()
@task_with_telemetry_context
def generate_deferred_payloads(
    self,
    event_delivery_ids: list,
    deferred_payload_data: dict,
    send_webhook_queue: str | None = None,
    *,
    telemetry_context: TelemetryTaskContext,
):
    """Build subscription payloads for deferred deliveries and send them.

    This task must not read the webhook's `payload_generation`. The deliveries it
    receives were created under the setting's value at trigger time, and a change
    made since must not alter how they complete.
    """
    if not event_delivery_ids:
        logger.warning(
            "No event delivery IDs provided for deferred payload generation task."
        )
        return

    task_properties = self.request.properties or {}
    message_group_id = task_properties.get("MessageGroupId")
    if message_group_id is None:
        domain = get_domain()
        message_group_id = get_sqs_message_group_id(domain, app=None)

    # Set up transaction to ensure that we always use the same
    # replica while checking the lag and generating the payloads.
    with transaction.atomic(
        using=settings.DATABASE_CONNECTION_REPLICA_NAME, savepoint=False
    ):
        db_connection_name = settings.DATABASE_CONNECTION_REPLICA_NAME
        available_delivery_pks, missing_delivery_pks = (
            confirm_event_delivery_availability(event_delivery_ids, db_connection_name)
        )

        if not available_delivery_pks:
            # If all deliveries are missing, we queue a retry to wait for replica
            try:
                retry_backoff = 1
                countdown = retry_backoff * (2**self.request.retries)
                raise self.retry(
                    countdown=countdown,
                    MessageGroupId=message_group_id,
                )
            except MaxRetriesExceededError:
                logger.error(
                    "Max retries exceeded for deferred payload generation. "
                    "Event deliveries not found on replica: %s.",
                    missing_delivery_pks,
                    extra={
                        "event_delivery_ids": event_delivery_ids,
                    },
                )
            return

        if missing_delivery_pks:
            # Process missing deliveries separately.
            request_kwargs = self.request.kwargs
            generate_deferred_payloads.apply_async(
                kwargs={
                    **request_kwargs,
                    "event_delivery_ids": list(missing_delivery_pks),
                },
                MessageGroupId=message_group_id,
            )

        _generate_deferred_payloads(
            event_delivery_ids=available_delivery_pks,
            deferred_payload_data=deferred_payload_data,
            send_webhook_queue=send_webhook_queue,
            telemetry_context=telemetry_context,
            database_connection_name=db_connection_name,
        )


def _generate_deferred_payloads(
    event_delivery_ids: set[int],
    deferred_payload_data: dict,
    send_webhook_queue: str | None,
    telemetry_context: TelemetryTaskContext,
    database_connection_name: str,
):
    deliveries = list(
        get_multiple_deliveries_for_webhooks(
            event_delivery_ids,
            database_connection_name=database_connection_name,
        )[0].values()
    )
    args_obj = DeferredPayloadData(**deferred_payload_data)
    requestor = None
    if args_obj.requestor_object_id and args_obj.requestor_model_name in (
        RequestorModelName.APP,
        RequestorModelName.USER,
    ):
        model = apps.get_model(args_obj.requestor_model_name)
        requestor = (
            model.objects.using(database_connection_name)
            .filter(pk=args_obj.requestor_object_id)
            .first()
        )

    if args_obj.subscribable_object_data is not None:
        event_type = deliveries[0].event_type
        subscribable_object = _reconstruct_subscribable_object(event_type, args_obj)
    elif args_obj.model_name and args_obj.object_id is not None:
        subscribable_object = (
            apps.get_model(args_obj.model_name)
            .objects.using(database_connection_name)
            .filter(pk=args_obj.object_id)
            .first()
        )
    else:
        subscribable_object = None
    if not subscribable_object:
        EventDelivery.objects.filter(pk__in=event_delivery_ids).update(
            status=EventDeliveryStatus.FAILED
        )
        return

    event_payloads = []
    event_payloads_data = []

    dataloaders: dict[str, type[DataLoader]] = {}
    request_map: dict[int, SaleorContext] = {}

    data_promises = []
    for delivery in deliveries:
        event_type = delivery.event_type
        webhook = delivery.webhook
        if not webhook.subscription_query:
            continue
        request = request_map.get(webhook.app_id)
        if not request:
            request = initialize_request(
                app=webhook.app,
                requestor=requestor,
                sync_event=event_type in WebhookEventSyncType.ALL,
                event_type=event_type,
                allow_replica=True,
                request_time=args_obj.request_time,
                dataloaders=dataloaders,
            )
            request_map[webhook.app_id] = request
        data_promises.append(
            generate_payload_promise_from_subscription(
                event_type=event_type,
                subscribable_object=subscribable_object,
                subscription_query=webhook.subscription_query,
                request=request,
            )
        )

    def with_subscription_payload(payloads):
        event_deliveries_for_bulk_update = []
        for data, delivery in zip(payloads, deliveries, strict=False):
            if data:
                data_json = json.dumps({**data})
                event_payloads_data.append(data_json)
                event_payload = EventPayload()
                event_payloads.append(event_payload)
                delivery.payload = event_payload
                event_deliveries_for_bulk_update.append(delivery)

        if event_deliveries_for_bulk_update:
            with allow_writer():
                with transaction.atomic():
                    EventPayload.objects.bulk_create_with_payload_files(
                        event_payloads, event_payloads_data
                    )
                    EventDelivery.objects.bulk_update(
                        event_deliveries_for_bulk_update, ["payload"]
                    )
        domain = get_domain()
        for delivery in event_deliveries_for_bulk_update:
            # Trigger webhook delivery task when the payload is ready.
            message_group_id = get_sqs_message_group_id(domain, delivery.webhook.app)
            # TODO: switch to new `send_webhooks_async_for_app` task when we have
            # deduplication mechanism in place.
            send_webhook_request_async.apply_async(
                kwargs={
                    "event_delivery_id": delivery.pk,
                    "telemetry_context": telemetry_context.to_dict(),
                },
                queue=get_queue_name_for_webhook(
                    delivery.webhook,
                    default_queue=send_webhook_queue
                    or settings.WEBHOOK_CELERY_QUEUE_NAME,
                ),
                MessageGroupId=message_group_id,  # for AWS SQS fair queues
            )

    Promise.all(data_promises).then(with_subscription_payload).get()
    return


def _reconstruct_subscribable_object(
    event_type: str,
    deferred_data: "DeferredPayloadData",
):
    """Reconstruct a dataclass subscribable object from serialized data.

    Looks up the expected dataclass from the event type mapping and instantiates
    it with the stored data. The dataclass constructor validates the structure —
    missing or unexpected fields will raise a TypeError.
    """
    data = deferred_data.subscribable_object_data
    if data is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "subscribable_object_data is required for "
            "dataclass-based deferred payloads."
        )
    cls = DEFERRED_SUBSCRIBABLE_OBJECT_MAP.get(event_type)
    if cls is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"No subscribable object class registered for event type: "
            f"{event_type}. Add it to DEFERRED_SUBSCRIBABLE_OBJECT_MAP."
        )
    try:
        return cls(**data)
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as e:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Failed to reconstruct {cls.__name__} from deferred payload data: {e}"
        ) from e


@app.task(
    queue=settings.WEBHOOK_CELERY_QUEUE_NAME,
    bind=True,
    retry_backoff=10,
    retry_kwargs={"max_retries": 5},
)
@allow_writer()
@task_with_telemetry_context
def send_webhook_request_async(
    self, event_delivery_id, *, telemetry_context: TelemetryTaskContext
) -> None:
    delivery, not_found = get_delivery_for_webhook(event_delivery_id)
    if not delivery:
        if not_found:
            raise self.retry(countdown=1)
        return

    webhook = delivery.webhook
    domain = get_domain()
    attempt = create_attempt(delivery, self.request.id)
    response = WebhookResponse(content="", status=EventDeliveryStatus.FAILED)
    retry_on_failure = False

    if not delivery.payload:
        response.content = f"Event delivery id: %{event_delivery_id}r has no payload."
    else:
        data = delivery.payload.get_payload()
        # Covert payload to bytes if it's not already.
        data = data if isinstance(data, bytes) else data.encode("utf-8")
        # Count payload size in bytes.
        payload_size = len(data)

        if self.request.retries == 0:
            record_first_delivery_attempt_delay(
                delivery.created_at, delivery.event_type, webhook.app
            )
        with webhooks_otel_trace(
            delivery.event_type,
            payload_size,
            webhook.app,
            span_links=telemetry_context.links,
        ) as span:
            try:
                response = send_webhook_using_scheme_method(
                    webhook.target_url,
                    domain,
                    webhook.secret_key,
                    delivery.event_type,
                    data,
                    webhook.custom_headers,
                )
                retry_on_failure = True
            except ValueError as e:
                response.content = str(e)
            if response.status == EventDeliveryStatus.FAILED:
                span.set_status(StatusCode.ERROR)
        record_external_request(
            delivery.event_type,
            webhook.target_url,
            response,
            payload_size,
            webhook.app,
            sync=False,
        )

    if response.status == EventDeliveryStatus.FAILED:
        attempt_update(attempt, response)
        if retry_on_failure:
            handle_webhook_retry(self, webhook, response, delivery, attempt)
        delivery_update(delivery, EventDeliveryStatus.FAILED)
    elif response.status == EventDeliveryStatus.SUCCESS:
        task_logger.info(
            "[Webhook ID:%r] Payload sent to %r for event %r. Delivery id: %r",
            webhook.id,
            sanitize_url_for_logging(webhook.target_url),
            delivery.event_type,
            delivery.id,
        )
        delivery.status = EventDeliveryStatus.SUCCESS
        # update attempt without save to provide proper data in observability
        attempt_update(attempt, response, with_save=False)
    observability.report_event_delivery_attempt(attempt)
    clear_successful_delivery(delivery)


@app.task(
    queue=settings.WEBHOOK_CELERY_QUEUE_NAME,
    bind=True,
)
@allow_writer()
@task_with_telemetry_context
def send_webhooks_async_for_app(
    self,
    app_id,
    telemetry_context: TelemetryTaskContext,
) -> None:
    domain = get_domain()
    deliveries = get_deliveries_for_app(app_id, WEBHOOK_ASYNC_BATCH_SIZE)

    if not deliveries:
        return

    attempts_for_deliveries = create_attempts_for_deliveries(
        deliveries, self.request.id
    )
    failed_deliveries_attempts = []
    successful_deliveries = []

    for delivery_id, delivery_with_count in deliveries.items():
        delivery = delivery_with_count.delivery
        attempt_count = delivery_with_count.count
        attempt = attempts_for_deliveries[delivery_id]

        webhook = delivery.webhook

        try:
            if not delivery.payload:
                raise ValueError(f"Event delivery id: {delivery_id} has no payload.")
            data = delivery.payload.get_payload()
            # Convert payload to bytes if it's not already.
            data = data if isinstance(data, bytes) else data.encode("utf-8")
            # Count payload size in bytes.
            payload_size = len(data)

            if attempt_count == 0:
                record_first_delivery_attempt_delay(
                    delivery.created_at, delivery.event_type, webhook.app
                )
            with webhooks_otel_trace(
                delivery.event_type,
                payload_size,
                webhook.app,
                span_links=telemetry_context.links,
            ):
                response = send_webhook_using_scheme_method(
                    webhook.target_url,
                    domain,
                    webhook.secret_key,
                    delivery.event_type,
                    data,
                    webhook.custom_headers,
                )

            record_external_request(
                delivery.event_type,
                webhook.target_url,
                response,
                payload_size,
                webhook.app,
                sync=False,
            )
            if response.status == EventDeliveryStatus.FAILED:
                attempt_update(attempt, response, with_save=False)
                failed_deliveries_attempts.append((delivery, attempt, attempt_count))
            elif response.status == EventDeliveryStatus.SUCCESS:
                task_logger.info(
                    "[Webhook ID:%r] Payload sent to %r for event %r. Delivery id: %r",
                    webhook.id,
                    sanitize_url_for_logging(webhook.target_url),
                    delivery.event_type,
                    delivery.id,
                )
                delivery.status = EventDeliveryStatus.SUCCESS
                # update attempt without save to provide proper data in observability
                attempt_update(attempt, response, with_save=False)
        except ValueError as e:
            response = WebhookResponse(
                content=str(e), status=EventDeliveryStatus.FAILED
            )
            attempt_update(attempt, response, with_save=False)
            failed_deliveries_attempts.append((delivery, attempt, attempt_count))

        observability.report_event_delivery_attempt(attempt)
        successful_deliveries.append(delivery)

    process_failed_deliveries(failed_deliveries_attempts, MAX_WEBHOOK_RETRIES)
    clear_successful_deliveries(successful_deliveries)

    send_webhooks_async_for_app.apply_async(
        kwargs={
            "app_id": app_id,
            "telemetry_context": telemetry_context.to_dict(),
        },
    )

578	def generate_deferred_payloads(
579	    self,
580	    event_delivery_ids: list,
581	    deferred_payload_data: dict,
582	    send_webhook_queue: str | None = None,
583	    *,
584	    telemetry_context: TelemetryTaskContext,
585	):
586	    """Build subscription payloads for deferred deliveries and send them.
587	
588	    This task must not read the webhook's `payload_generation`. The deliveries it
589	    receives were created under the setting's value at trigger time, and a change
590	    made since must not alter how they complete.
591	    """
592	    if not event_delivery_ids:
593	        logger.warning(
594	            "No event delivery IDs provided for deferred payload generation task."
595	        )
596	        return
597	
598	    task_properties = self.request.properties or {}
599	    message_group_id = task_properties.get("MessageGroupId")
600	    if message_group_id is None:
601	        domain = get_domain()
602	        message_group_id = get_sqs_message_group_id(domain, app=None)
603	
604	    # Set up transaction to ensure that we always use the same
605	    # replica while checking the lag and generating the payloads.
606	    with transaction.atomic(
607	        using=settings.DATABASE_CONNECTION_REPLICA_NAME, savepoint=False
608	    ):
609	        db_connection_name = settings.DATABASE_CONNECTION_REPLICA_NAME
610	        available_delivery_pks, missing_delivery_pks = (
611	            confirm_event_delivery_availability(event_delivery_ids, db_connection_name)
612	        )
613	
614	        if not available_delivery_pks:
615	            # If all deliveries are missing, we queue a retry to wait for replica
616	            try:
617	                retry_backoff = 1
618	                countdown = retry_backoff * (2**self.request.retries)
619	                raise self.retry(
620	                    countdown=countdown,
621	                    MessageGroupId=message_group_id,
622	                )
623	            except MaxRetriesExceededError:
624	                logger.error(
625	                    "Max retries exceeded for deferred payload generation. "
626	                    "Event deliveries not found on replica: %s.",
627	                    missing_delivery_pks,
628	                    extra={
629	                        "event_delivery_ids": event_delivery_ids,
630	                    },
631	                )
632	            return
633	
634	        if missing_delivery_pks:
635	            # Process missing deliveries separately.
636	            request_kwargs = self.request.kwargs
637	            generate_deferred_payloads.apply_async(
638	                kwargs={
639	                    **request_kwargs,
640	                    "event_delivery_ids": list(missing_delivery_pks),
641	                },
642	                MessageGroupId=message_group_id,
643	            )
644	
645	        _generate_deferred_payloads(
646	            event_delivery_ids=available_delivery_pks,
647	            deferred_payload_data=deferred_payload_data,
648	            send_webhook_queue=send_webhook_queue,
649	            telemetry_context=telemetry_context,
650	            database_connection_name=db_connection_name,
651	        )

666	    )
667	    args_obj = DeferredPayloadData(**deferred_payload_data)
668	    requestor = None
669	    if args_obj.requestor_object_id and args_obj.requestor_model_name in (
670	        RequestorModelName.APP,
671	        RequestorModelName.USER,
672	    ):
673	        model = apps.get_model(args_obj.requestor_model_name)
674	        requestor = (

677	            .first()
678	        )
679	
680	    if args_obj.subscribable_object_data is not None:
681	        event_type = deliveries[0].event_type

683	    elif args_obj.model_name and args_obj.object_id is not None:
684	        subscribable_object = (
685	            apps.get_model(args_obj.model_name)
686	            .objects.using(database_connection_name)
687	            .filter(pk=args_obj.object_id)
688	            .first()
689	        )
690	    else:
691	        subscribable_object = None
692	    if not subscribable_object:
693	        EventDelivery.objects.filter(pk__in=event_delivery_ids).update(
694	            status=EventDeliveryStatus.FAILED
695	        )
696	        return
697	
698	    event_payloads = []
699	    event_payloads_data = []
700	
701	    dataloaders: dict[str, type[DataLoader]] = {}
702	    request_map: dict[int, SaleorContext] = {}
703	
704	    data_promises = []
705	    for delivery in deliveries:
706	        event_type = delivery.event_type
707	        webhook = delivery.webhook
708	        if not webhook.subscription_query:
709	            continue
710	        request = request_map.get(webhook.app_id)
711	        if not request:
712	            request = initialize_request(
713	                app=webhook.app,
714	                requestor=requestor,
715	                sync_event=event_type in WebhookEventSyncType.ALL,
716	                event_type=event_type,
717	                allow_replica=True,
718	                request_time=args_obj.request_time,
719	                dataloaders=dataloaders,
720	            )
721	            request_map[webhook.app_id] = request
722	        data_promises.append(
723	            generate_payload_promise_from_subscription(
724	                event_type=event_type,
725	                subscribable_object=subscribable_object,
726	                subscription_query=webhook.subscription_query,
727	                request=request,
728	            )
729	        )

731	    def with_subscription_payload(payloads):
732	        event_deliveries_for_bulk_update = []
733	        for data, delivery in zip(payloads, deliveries, strict=False):
734	            if data:
735	                data_json = json.dumps({**data})
736	                event_payloads_data.append(data_json)
737	                event_payload = EventPayload()
738	                event_payloads.append(event_payload)
739	                delivery.payload = event_payload
740	                event_deliveries_for_bulk_update.append(delivery)
741	
742	        if event_deliveries_for_bulk_update:
743	            with allow_writer():
744	                with transaction.atomic():
745	                    EventPayload.objects.bulk_create_with_payload_files(
746	                        event_payloads, event_payloads_data
747	                    )
748	                    EventDelivery.objects.bulk_update(
749	                        event_deliveries_for_bulk_update, ["payload"]
750	                    )
751	        domain = get_domain()
752	        for delivery in event_deliveries_for_bulk_update:
753	            # Trigger webhook delivery task when the payload is ready.
754	            message_group_id = get_sqs_message_group_id(domain, delivery.webhook.app)
755	            # TODO: switch to new `send_webhooks_async_for_app` task when we have
756	            # deduplication mechanism in place.
757	            send_webhook_request_async.apply_async(
758	                kwargs={
759	                    "event_delivery_id": delivery.pk,

766	                ),
767	                MessageGroupId=message_group_id,  # for AWS SQS fair queues

775	    event_type: str,
776	    deferred_data: "DeferredPayloadData",
777	):
778	    """Reconstruct a dataclass subscribable object from serialized data.
779	
780	    Looks up the expected dataclass from the event type mapping and instantiates
781	    it with the stored data. The dataclass constructor validates the structure —
782	    missing or unexpected fields will raise a TypeError.
783	    """
784	    data = deferred_data.subscribable_object_data
785	    if data is None:
786	        raise ValueError(
787	            "subscribable_object_data is required for "

794	            f"{event_type}. Add it to DEFERRED_SUBSCRIBABLE_OBJECT_MAP."
795	        )
796	    try:
797	        return cls(**data)
798	    except (TypeError, ValueError) as e:
799	        raise ValueError(
800	            f"Failed to reconstruct {cls.__name__} from deferred payload data: {e}"
801	        ) from e

def get_multiple_deliveries_for_webhooks(
    event_delivery_ids,
    database_connection_name: str = settings.DATABASE_CONNECTION_DEFAULT_NAME,
) -> tuple[dict[int, "EventDelivery"], set[int]]:
    deliveries = (
        EventDelivery.objects.using(database_connection_name)
        .select_related("payload", "webhook__app")
        .filter(id__in=event_delivery_ids)
    )

    active_deliveries = {}
    inactive_delivery_ids = set()

    not_found_delivery_ids = set(event_delivery_ids) - {
        delivery.pk for delivery in deliveries
    }
    for not_found_delivery_id in not_found_delivery_ids:
        logger.warning("Event delivery id: %r not found", not_found_delivery_id)

    for delivery in deliveries:
        # For these 2 apps will (if deleted) or can (if deactivated) be inactive at this point
        # For these two, we bypass active app check and emit anyway
        bypass_inactive_check = delivery.event_type in (
            WebhookEventAsyncType.APP_DELETED,
            WebhookEventAsyncType.APP_STATUS_CHANGED,
        )
        should_deliver = delivery.webhook.is_active and (
            delivery.webhook.app.is_active or bypass_inactive_check
        )

        if should_deliver:
            active_deliveries[delivery.pk] = delivery
        else:
            logger.info("Event delivery id: %r app/webhook is disabled.", delivery.pk)
            inactive_delivery_ids.add(delivery.pk)

    if inactive_delivery_ids:
        EventDelivery.objects.filter(id__in=inactive_delivery_ids).update(
            status=EventDeliveryStatus.FAILED
        )

    return active_deliveries, inactive_delivery_ids

def get_multiple_deliveries_for_webhooks(
    event_delivery_ids,
    database_connection_name: str = settings.DATABASE_CONNECTION_DEFAULT_NAME,
) -> tuple[dict[int, "EventDelivery"], set[int]]:
    deliveries = (
        EventDelivery.objects.using(database_connection_name)
        .select_related("payload", "webhook__app")
        .filter(id__in=event_delivery_ids)
    )

    active_deliveries = {}
    inactive_delivery_ids = set()

    not_found_delivery_ids = set(event_delivery_ids) - {
        delivery.pk for delivery in deliveries
    }
    for not_found_delivery_id in not_found_delivery_ids:
        logger.warning("Event delivery id: %r not found", not_found_delivery_id)

    for delivery in deliveries:
        # For these 2 apps will (if deleted) or can (if deactivated) be inactive at this point
        # For these two, we bypass active app check and emit anyway
        bypass_inactive_check = delivery.event_type in (
            WebhookEventAsyncType.APP_DELETED,
            WebhookEventAsyncType.APP_STATUS_CHANGED,
        )
        should_deliver = delivery.webhook.is_active and (
            delivery.webhook.app.is_active or bypass_inactive_check
        )

        if should_deliver:
            active_deliveries[delivery.pk] = delivery
        else:
            logger.info("Event delivery id: %r app/webhook is disabled.", delivery.pk)
            inactive_delivery_ids.add(delivery.pk)

    if inactive_delivery_ids:
        EventDelivery.objects.filter(id__in=inactive_delivery_ids).update(
            status=EventDeliveryStatus.FAILED
        )

    return active_deliveries, inactive_delivery_ids

=== ADR 0004
# Balance adjustments must be race-safe and free of TOCTOU issues

**Tags:** gift card, concurrency

Changing a gift card's balance is money movement that can happen concurrently — a staff adjustment and a checkout charge can hit the same card at the same time. Any balance operation must therefore be **atomic** and free of time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) races: never read a balance, decide, and write it back as separate steps, because a concurrent operation can invalidate the decision in between and silently lose an update or overspend the card.

Practically, this means balance changes are expressed as a single atomic operation (an adjustment applied directly at the database level, self-clamping so a card can never go negative) rather than a read-modify-write in application code. Because this cannot be done safely through the ordinary "load, edit fields, save" update path, balance adjustment is a dedicated operation rather than another editable field on the general gift-card update. This rule applies to any future balance-changing operation, not just the current one.
=== ADR 0010
# Order payment history is a projection, not an opened `TransactionItem`

**Tags:** payments, graphql, permissions, orders

Customer-facing payment history is a new `Order.transactionSummaries` field returning a
`TransactionSummary` projection of the existing `TransactionItem` rows, rather than a permission
change on `Order.transactions`.

Opening `Order.transactions` would publish the whole type — `externalUrl` (PSP back-office deep
link), `events` (internal ledger, staff identities, idempotency keys), `createdBy`, `name`,
`message` — and its `id`, which is the transaction `token`, a capability accepted by the
unauthenticated `transactionInitialize`/`transactionProcess` mutations. Allowlisting fields on the
existing type is not an option either: `PermissionsField` raises, and `[TransactionItem!]!` with
non-null fields means one denied field nulls the entire order. The projection is an allowlist, so
fields added to `TransactionItem` later cannot leak through it.

The field is meant to be queried by a storefront (account page, order summary) to show the money
that moved to and from the customer. That is why transactions with all amounts at zero are
filtered out: they are abandoned payment attempts and carry no information for the customer.

Card data is stripped for the same reason. `paymentMethodDetails` reuses the shared
`PaymentMethodDetails` types, but the resolver blanks `firstDigits`, `lastDigits`, `expMonth` and
`expYear` on a copy of the transaction, so a public caller sees the payment method and the brand
and nothing that identifies the instrument. Staff read the full card data through
`Order.transactions` as before.

Because this cannot be done safely through the ordinary "load, edit fields, save" update path, balance adjustment is a dedicated operation rather than another editable field on the general gift-card update. This rule applies to any future balance-changing operation, not just the current one.
=== ADR 0010
# Order payment history is a projection, not an opened `TransactionItem`

**Tags:** payments, graphql, permissions, orders

Customer-facing payment history is a new `Order.transactionSummaries` field returning a
`TransactionSummary` projection of the existing `TransactionItem` rows, rather than a permission
change on `Order.transactions`.

Opening `Order.transactions` would publish the whole type — `externalUrl` (PSP back-office deep
link), `events` (internal ledger, staff identities, idempotency keys), `createdBy`, `name`,
`message` — and its `id`, which is the transaction `token`, a capability accepted by the
unauthenticated `transactionInitialize`/`transactionProcess` mutations. Allowlisting fields on the
existing type is not an option either: `PermissionsField` raises, and `[TransactionItem!]!` with
non-null fields means one denied field nulls the entire order. The projection is an allowlist, so
fields added to `TransactionItem` later cannot leak through it.

The field is meant to be queried by a storefront (account page, order summary) to show the money
that moved to and from the customer. That is why transactions with all amounts at zero are
filtered out: they are abandoned payment attempts and carry no information for the customer.

Card data is stripped for the same reason. `paymentMethodDetails` reuses the shared
`PaymentMethodDetails` types, but the resolver blanks `firstDigits`, `lastDigits`, `expMonth` and
`expYear` on a copy of the transaction, so a public caller sees the payment method and the brand
and nothing that identifies the instrument. Staff read the full card data through
`Order.transactions` as before.

Webhook behaviour that is intended

Withdrawn from the register after review against ADR 0011 and Saleor's webhook documentation. These are documented contracts or deployment settings, not problems, and they are not counted above. They stay on this page because the integrations and the deployment have to be built to them.

Deferred payloads show the object's current state

For order, draft order, fulfillment, checkout and per-channel stock and price events, a subscription webhook's payload is built by a background task after the request, so it shows the object as it is at that moment. Two quick changes can produce two identical deliveries. A webhook opts out by setting payloadGeneration to IMMEDIATE through webhookCreate, webhookUpdate or the app manifest. Legacy webhooks without a subscription query always carry request-time state.

Was part of WH-5. docs/adr/0011; schema.graphql:14604-14607,23167,23237

A deleted object gives a failed delivery and no webhook

If the object is deleted before the deferred payload is built, the delivery is marked failed and nothing is sent. The ADR records this as an accepted consequence. The rows this leaves behind are a separate matter, in WH-10.

Was part of WH-10. docs/adr/0011

Order is not guaranteed and an event can arrive twice

Saleor's documentation states that the order of arrival is not guaranteed in either payload mode, and a delivery is retried when the endpoint does not answer in time, so a slow receiver can get the same event again. No delivery id is sent. A subscription query can ask for issuedAt, which is the time of the request that raised the event.

Was WH-5. docs.saleor.io asynchronous-events; saleor/app/headers.py; saleor/graphql/webhook/subscription_types.py:143-144

Inactive apps and webhooks receive nothing

While an app or webhook is inactive no delivery is recorded for it, and reactivating replays nothing. Deliveries already queued are marked failed and can be retried by hand. This is what deactivation means, and webhookDelete deactivates the webhook first for the same reason.

Was WH-11. saleor/webhook/utils.py:44-66; saleor/webhook/transport/utils.py:493-513

Payload files need shared private storage

Payloads are written as files to private storage, which is the local file system until a private bucket is set. With several pods that setting is a deployment prerequisite: AWS_MEDIA_PRIVATE_BUCKET_NAME, GS_MEDIA_PRIVATE_BUCKET_NAME or AZURE_CONTAINER_PRIVATE. What happens when a payload file cannot be read is a defect and stays in WH-2.

Was WH-3. saleor/settings.py:589-595

Targets on private addresses are refused

The IP filter is a security control that rejects webhook targets resolving to private ranges, such as an in-cluster ERP. HTTP_IP_FILTER_ENABLED and HTTP_IP_FILTER_ALLOW_LOOPBACK_IPS change it for the whole installation. Separately, FIFO SQS targets get one message group per domain and no deduplication id; the AWS side of that was not tested.

Was WH-13. saleor/settings.py:965-974; saleor/webhook/transport/utils.py:766-791

Webhook behaviour that is intended

Withdrawn from the register after review against ADR 0011 and Saleor's webhook documentation. These are documented contracts or deployment settings, not problems, and they are not counted above. They stay on this page because the integrations and the deployment have to be built to them.

Deferred payloads show the object's current state

For order, draft order, fulfillment, checkout and per-channel stock and price events, a subscription webhook's payload is built by a background task after the request, so it shows the object as it is at that moment. Two quick changes can produce two identical deliveries. A webhook opts out by setting payloadGeneration to IMMEDIATE through webhookCreate, webhookUpdate or the app manifest. Legacy webhooks without a subscription query always carry request-time state.

Was part of WH-5. docs/adr/0011; schema.graphql:14604-14607,23167,23237

A deleted object gives a failed delivery and no webhook

If the object is deleted before the deferred payload is built, the delivery is marked failed and nothing is sent. The ADR records this as an accepted consequence. The rows this leaves behind are a separate matter, in WH-10.

Was part of WH-10. docs/adr/0011

Order is not guaranteed and an event can arrive twice

Saleor's documentation states that the order of arrival is not guaranteed in either payload mode, and a delivery is retried when the endpoint does not answer in time, so a slow receiver can get the same event again. No delivery id is sent. A subscription query can ask for issuedAt, which is the time of the request that raised the event.

Was WH-5. docs.saleor.io asynchronous-events; saleor/app/headers.py; saleor/graphql/webhook/subscription_types.py:143-144

Inactive apps and webhooks receive nothing

While an app or webhook is inactive no delivery is recorded for it, and reactivating replays nothing. Deliveries already queued are marked failed and can be retried by hand. This is what deactivation means, and webhookDelete deactivates the webhook first for the same reason.

Was WH-11. saleor/webhook/utils.py:44-66; saleor/webhook/transport/utils.py:493-513

Payload files need shared private storage

Payloads are written as files to private storage, which is the local file system until a private bucket is set. With several pods that setting is a deployment prerequisite: AWS_MEDIA_PRIVATE_BUCKET_NAME, GS_MEDIA_PRIVATE_BUCKET_NAME or AZURE_CONTAINER_PRIVATE. What happens when a payload file cannot be read is a defect and stays in WH-2.

Was WH-3. saleor/settings.py:589-595

Targets on private addresses are refused

The IP filter is a security control that rejects webhook targets resolving to private ranges, such as an in-cluster ERP. HTTP_IP_FILTER_ENABLED and HTTP_IP_FILTER_ALLOW_LOOPBACK_IPS change it for the whole installation. Separately, FIFO SQS targets get one message group per domain and no deduplication id; the AWS side of that was not tested.

Was WH-13. saleor/settings.py:965-974; saleor/webhook/transport/utils.py:766-791

**Withdrawn as problems** (moved to a new, uncounted section, "Webhook behaviour that is intended"):

- **WH-5:** deferred payloads carrying current state is the ADR's accepted consequence, with the `IMMEDIATE` opt-out. Unordered arrival and repeat deliveries after a timeout are the documented delivery contract.
- **WH-11:** inactive apps and webhooks receiving nothing is what deactivation means.
- **WH-3:** local-disk payload storage is a default that a private bucket setting replaces, so it is a deployment prerequisite rather than a problem.
- **WH-13:** refusing private-address targets is a security control with its own settings.

**Amended:**

- **WH-10:** the "failed delivery when the object is deleted" claim is removed, since the ADR defines it as intended. What remains is not in the ADR: deliveries that never get a payload are never cleaned up, and some stay pending for good. Lowered from medium to low.
- **WH-1:** the retry policy (five retries, none on 3xx or 4xx) is documented and intended, and the entry now says so. I kept it because no setting changes the retry count, so after a longer outage staff must retry failed deliveries one at a time. It also now notes that the 14-day retention is configurable.
- **WH-8:** narrowed. Sharing the default queue is a configuration choice; the part with no setting is that a hanging target delays deliveries to every other app.
- **WH-2:** picks up the one real defect from the old WH-3: an unreadable payload file leaves the delivery pending with no retry.
- **WH-12:** re-checked against the code; wording unchanged.

Every remaining webhook entry now has a "Design status" line saying whether the behaviour is intended, and on what source. WH-7 (staff screens waiting up to 20 seconds on a slow app) is marked as intended and kept for the same reason as WH-1. WH-6 (shipping filter failing open) is marked "not stated either way", because neither the ADRs nor the shipping-webhook docs say what should happen.

Decision for you: WH-1 and WH-7 are still counted as problems even though the behaviour is intended, because nothing switches it off and staff bear the consequence. If you want the register to hold only unintended behaviour, say so and I'll move both to the intended section.

skills.name: artifact-design
skills.content:
Work the way the design lead at a small, versatile studio would: give each client a visual identity at the level of treatment the task calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Decide the treatment; designing is a given. A doc gets the same craft as a landing page; only the treatment differs. Format is a separate matter: author HTML, and publish Markdown only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it. A Markdown publish keeps its filename as its title, uses almost none of the craft below, and is never a way to save time.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished, with real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages don't need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

If unsure: a well-composed page is always acceptable; an over-designed visual identity sometimes isn't.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. Follow the editorial process after them only when that reading calls for it.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Respect what already exists.** Look for an existing design system first: CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, define it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. Distinctive choices come from the subject's own world: its materials, instruments, and vernacular. Whatever the treatment, include at least one detail only this subject would have (its real units and scales, its document conventions, its terms of art) as content rather than ornament; it costs nothing even on a plain page. Use real content throughout and never lorem ipsum.

**Pair typefaces.** Typography determines how the page reads even when the page isn't about typography. Inter for text and Space Grotesk for headings are good defaults when nothing in the request or the subject calls for other type. Google Fonts is the only font host the Artifact CSP allows; link it directly (`<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=...&display=swap">`). A face from anywhere else must be inlined as a @font-face data URI, or the browser silently uses a fallback. In both cases, declare a real fallback stack. Keep running text near 65 characters wide. Set a type scale and keep to it. Give headings `text-wrap: balance`, give body text comfortable spacing, and give uppercase labels a little letter-spacing.
